business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Positions itself as an integrated design-engineering-manufacturing partner: "Precision sheet-metal stamping, robotic welded assemblies and complex automotive sub-assemblies" plus "Integrated design-to-manufacturing: engineering, tooling, fixtures, process validation, quality systems and serial production".
- Claims to be "Anchored in leading OEM programmes across PV, CV and EV-linked platforms", with "Design company capability supports engineering-led growth and early customer engagement".
- Names a marquee clientele list including Ashok Leyland (Dost, Bada Dost, Partner), Daimler (Bharat Benz) 9T/12T, Tata-Hitachi EX220, Sany SY 220 and Hyundai R140 LC9, plus non-auto customers.
- Frames the transition as "Autoline has moved from recovery orientation to disciplined scale-up with stronger customer relevance, operational leverage and governance-led execution".

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- "Balance-sheet focus - Autoline Industrial Park Ltd. monetisation and cash discipline improved the platform for the next phase."
- "Balance-sheet management - Capex phasing, debt optimisation, current ratio improvement and capital allocation discipline."
- "Group consolidation - Consolidate group businesses where value leakage or structural burden exists; improve focus and accountability."
- FY27 is to be "reviewed as a conversion plan: opportunity - capacity - production - dispatch - receivables - cash"; no dividend or buyback policy is mentioned.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Event] The deck is the Investor Meet Presentation filed under Regulation 30 for a meet on 10 July 2026 at Hotel Grand Hyatt, Mumbai, and is marked "Public Disclosure | No UPSI intended".
- [Basis of information] The deck states it is "based on publicly available financial information, approved business priorities and management assessment", and that "FY27 outlook and growth-related statements should be read as management estimates / business outlook and not as a guarantee or assurance of future performance".
